prompt: Build a producer/consumer pipeline: one thread feeds a capacity-2 BlockingQueue, another drains it until it sees a poison pill. Complete drain, then run the tests.
explanation: A BlockingQueue is the hand-off point between threads: put() waits when the queue is full and take() waits when it is empty, so neither side needs locks or sleeps. The poison pill is a sentinel value the producer sends after the real work, telling the consumer that no more items are coming -- without it the consumer would block on take() forever. Joining both threads before returning guarantees the collected list is complete and safely visible to the calling thread.
hints: new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(2) gives you the queue; the producer loops over items calling queue.put(item) and then puts POISON once at the end.
The consumer loops forever on take(), and the pill is its only exit: compare each value against POISON and return the moment they match, otherwise add the upper-cased value to the list.
Start both threads, then join() both BEFORE you return the list; the join is what makes the consumer's writes visible to the caller.
